definitionOfDone: Three-quarter and side renders read as the same village well: individual ashlar ring, deep opening, timber gantry, tiled canopy, riveted windlass, crank, rope and bucket.
All child systems visibly contact their parent and the visible sole remains at y=0.

proceduralStrategy: Build individual chamfered ashlar modules rather than a cylinder texture.
Use a closed indexed gable shell plus repeated curved tile relief.
Use named timber/frame/windlass/bucket runtime groups with explicit sockets.
Use tube geometry only for crank and rope paths; use torus repetition for rope coils.
lightingFromPhoto: Warm-neutral key light from upper-front-right at intensity near 3.2 defines stone chamfers, tile curvature and wood frame contacts.
Cool-neutral fill from upper-left near 0.8 preserves the dark shaft, bucket and back faces.
Warm rear rim near 1.0 separates the broad clay roof and dark hardware from a light warm-gray background.
Use ACES filmic tone mapping at exposure near 1.1 and a soft contact ground shadow under the masonry sole.
